defects: Core hypothesis is wrong: gold assumes `IsSetSemiring C`, whose defining content is ∅ ∈ C, closure under finite intersection, and that s \ t for s,t ∈ C decomposes into a finite disjoint union of members of C (diff_mem_disjUnion). The produced statement instead assumes closure under arbitrary finite union (h_union) plus intersection (h_inter) and ∅ ∈ R — this is a different, non-equivalent structure (closer to a lattice/ring of sets), not the standard 'semiring of sets' referenced in the informal statement.

A semiring of sets need not be closed under union (e.g. half-open intervals), so h_union is an added/incorrect hypothesis not implied by IsSetSemiring; conversely IsSetSemiring's actual defining decomposition property (diff_mem_disjUnion) is dropped entirely.

Because no closure under set difference/complement is assumed, the produced hypotheses (union+intersection closure) are not obviously sufficient to derive the stated conclusion, indicating the formalization mismatches the intended semiring-of-sets result rather than merely restating it differently.
